overview.process: Amazon's interview process typically consists of: (1) Resume screen, (2) Online Assessment (2 coding + work style survey), (3) Phone screen with coding, (4) Virtual On-site (4–5 loops of 45 min each).
overview.codingEnvironment: Amazon uses a custom online coding platform. Java, Python, C++, JavaScript supported.
overview.timeline: Total process: 2–6 weeks from application to offer.

leadershipPrinciples.name: Customer Obsession
leadershipPrinciples.question: Tell me about a time you went above and beyond for a customer.
leadershipPrinciples.angle: Focus on the impact to the end customer — not just your manager. Quantify satisfaction or retention improvement.

leadershipPrinciples.name: Ownership
leadershipPrinciples.question: Tell me about a time you took ownership of a problem that wasn't technically yours.
leadershipPrinciples.angle: Show initiative beyond your job description. Amazon wants engineers who own outcomes, not just tasks.

leadershipPrinciples.name: Invent and Simplify
leadershipPrinciples.question: Tell me about a time you found a simpler solution to a complex problem.
leadershipPrinciples.angle: The simplification should be technically concrete — reduced lines of code, eliminated a dependency, merged two systems.

leadershipPrinciples.name: Dive Deep
leadershipPrinciples.question: Tell me about a time you had to dig deep into a problem to find the root cause.
leadershipPrinciples.angle: Walk through your debugging process methodically. Amazon wants to hear about the data you gathered, hypotheses you tested.

leadershipPrinciples.name: Deliver Results
leadershipPrinciples.question: Tell me about a time you delivered a project under significant constraints.
leadershipPrinciples.angle: Use numbers: '30% ahead of schedule', 'saved $500k in infrastructure costs'. Always quantify.

systemDesignFavorites: Design S3 (or a distributed file storage system)

dsaFocus.difficulty: Mostly medium. Hard questions appear in senior+ roles.
dsaFocus.note: Amazon values clear communication of approach before coding. Explain your plan, get buy-in, then code.
